Answered — the objectui walk was taken, and the reader exists. Recording the full reading before closing. ## Provenance A read-only objectui checkout became reachable mid-session at a non-standard path (`/home/user/objectstack-ai/objectui`); the dispatching PM seat pointed at it and supplied two candidate lines, which I verified myself rather than adopting. All readings below are `git -C … show/grep origin/main`, never a working tree. Zero writes to objectui, no worktree there. Measured at objectui `origin/main@26896c6` (tip on 2026-08-29). The PM's reading was taken at `d06059f`; that commit **is an ancestor** of the tip, and `ToolPreview.tsx` is byte-identical at both (blob `df3d5132e28d228396699beb82d7a632c2822415`), so the reading is stable across the two shas. ## The reader `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/ToolPreview.tsx`, in `ToolPreview`: ```tsx const objectName = (d.objectName as string | undefined) || undefined; ... {objectName && (
)} ``` `d` is the persisted tool record's body. Registered as the `tool` type's preview (`previews/index.ts`, `registerMetadataPreview('tool', ToolPreview)`), and the registration is resolved and handed a draft by `ResourceEditPage.tsx` via `getMetadataPreview(type)` — so the read point is **reachable**, not merely present, which is the half the #7131 rule insists on citing. It is also **deliberately pinned**. `ToolPreview.test.tsx` asserts the pill renders and that the row disappears when the key is removed, over a comment reading: > `objectName` is NOT residue — ToolSchema still accepts it. I searched objectui for any *other*, behavioural consumer and found none: the only other file holding both a tool token and `objectName` is `clientValidation.ts`, whose `objectName` is derived from `d.name` and has nothing to do with this key. ## Verdict: `live` as a DISPLAY key — and the reasoning inverts, not the verdict Both halves are now on the record, and each is load-bearing: 1. **The old basis stays falsified.** The row claimed "action-tool dispatch". Both cited cloud sites read `action.objectName` (the ActionSchema key, whose `action.json` row carries that citation verbatim), and the same-named `AIToolDefinition.objectName` is written by `actionToToolDefinition` and read by nothing in cloud or framework. The key gates, binds and routes **nothing**. 2. **A real consumer exists on the other basis** — the metadata read-back. Under #7131 that settles a *display* key, and for authored tool metadata the render is not standing in for a behaviour, because `ToolSchema`'s own describe says a metadata-authored tool is a read-only projection no executor loads. There is no second layer for the preview to proxy. So `live` stands, as display and never as a binding, and the entry now says exactly that. **Explicitly not an ADR-0049 retirement candidate**: a `dead` verdict would have retired a key the renderer deliberately renders and tests — the `requiresService` / `colorVariant` lesson from the other end. The previous pass's refusal to grade `dead` while objectui was unreachable was the right call; the renderer was where the answer lived. ## Wider correction this forced `tool.json`'s `_note` claimed for years that tool metadata is "WRITE-ONLY … not metadata read-back". That is false, and it is precisely why nobody looked at the renderer. `ToolPreview` reads **all six** props off the stored record — `name`, `label`, `description`, `objectName`, `parameters`, `outputSchema`. The type has two live bases (the `AIToolDefinition` surface, behavioural; and the metadata read-back, display), and every row now names the one it rests on. Landed on PR #13275 at `4bc1737c` (branch `claude/issue-13042-tool-liveness-reclose`, still draft). Liveness family green on that commit: `verifiedAt` 452 to 453 (all six entries now dated, 0 undated in this file), cross-repo scope 69 to 70, producers 15 to 16, and `state-counts.md is current` — no verdict moved, so the counts are untouched. Closing as answered. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_
